answer: Each agent, chosen randomly quarterly, assesses 10 non-kin peers' identities, staking 5 umber coins. If any peer is flagged as a sybil, the staked umber is burned; if none are sybil, the umber is returned. An attacker running N identities pays 5N umber coins per quarter for each potential colluder caught, while honest agents risk only 5 umber per assessment. Hollow identities, unable to mirror real ones' diverse actions, fail the honeypot test, exposing colluders.
